selection_reason: largest CER decrease of any method in group dark (edit distance 5 -> 2)
visual_observation: Very dark plate (CCPD brightness 21). Homomorphic lifts the characters off the dark background without saturating them; CLAHE brightens less. JPEG 8x8 blocks become visible in the background but do not cross the strokes.

selection_reason: all three methods reduce edit distance (4 -> 2) in group mid
visual_observation: Dim yellowish plate. All methods raise character/background contrast; Top/Black-Hat gives the strongest stroke contrast but also the strongest block artefacts around the characters.

selection_reason: largest CER decrease in group bright (edit distance 7 -> 4)
visual_observation: Glare-washed plate. CLAHE restores local contrast on the non-saturated characters (X6S). The left (province+A) and the last character stay saturated in every method: clipped pixels carry no information to recover.

selection_reason: identical OCR for all four variants
visual_observation: Original is already well exposed and readable. All methods keep the same 6 alphanumeric characters; the only error in every variant is the missing Chinese province character (Tesseract limitation, not illumination).
Whole plate is overexposed: white characters on a near-white background. No method recovers the strokes, the information is lost at capture (saturation).

selection_reason: largest CER increase (edit distance 3 -> 7) in the test set
visual_observation: Dark plate with strong JPEG blocking. Top/Black-Hat and Homomorphic amplify the block edges inside the characters '86', breaking stroke continuity; OCR loses most characters.

Bright plate. Top/Black-Hat produces dark halos and double outlines along character edges and the plate frame. Homomorphic flattens the bright plate to a grey haze, lowering character/background contrast.

selection_reason: Homomorphic edit distance 5 -> 7 on the darkest plate (CCPD brightness 6)
visual_observation: Extremely dark plate. Homomorphic normalisation stretches sensor noise and JPEG blocks into visible grey texture and halos around strokes; OCR output becomes unrelated letters.
